title: How OneCoin sold a coin that never existed

hook.belief: Nobody would pour real money into a coin that does not exist; millions of buyers must have been sold real technology.
hook.gap: If the coin was never real, what were millions of people actually buying?

scenes.narration: Would you hand your savings to a coin that never existed? Millions did, and OneCoin raised over four billion dollars.
scenes.visual_intent: A gold coin spins up as an investment, then is shown to be a flat drawing with nothing behind it.
scenes.visualMetaphor: A glowing gold coin turns edge-on and is revealed as a paper-thin cutout with nothing behind it.

facts.claim: OneCoin took in more than $4 billion from victims worldwide between 2014 and 2016.
Millions of people worldwide invested in OneCoin.

scenes.narration: A real crypto coin lives on a public ledger: thousands of copies, so nobody can fake a balance.
scenes.visual_intent: One ledger page is copied everywhere, so a forged line is caught by every copy at once.
scenes.visualMetaphor: One ledger page fans out into a wall of identical copies; a forged row flashes red on every copy.

facts.claim: Bitcoin records transactions in a public ledger (a blockchain) that many independent nodes hold and verify, so a forged balance is rejected.
facts.source: Nakamoto, S. (2008). Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System. https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf

scenes.narration: But OneCoin kept its ledger private. [PAUSE 0.9s] Prosecutors say there was no real blockchain, and its bosses handed out coins that existed nowhere.
scenes.visual_intent: The wall of public copies goes dark, leaving one locked notebook that someone simply types numbers into.
scenes.visualMetaphor: The wall of copies goes dark; one locked private notebook remains and a hand types balances into it.

facts.claim: Prosecutors say OneCoin had no true, verifiable blockchain.
Greenwood and Ignatova allocated to members OneCoins that did not exist even in OneCoin's purported private blockchain.

scenes.narration: Yet millions believed, because Dr Ruja Ignatova filled Wembley Arena in 2016 and sold OneCoin as the bitcoin killer.
scenes.visual_intent: A packed arena lights up for one confident founder on stage, and credibility does the selling.
scenes.visualMetaphor: Arena spotlights sweep and lock on a podium while thousands of phone lights rise in the crowd.

facts.claim: In the summer of 2016 Ruja Ignatova took the stage at Wembley Arena and promoted OneCoin as the bitcoin killer.
Ruja Ignatova was dubbed the Cryptoqueen.

scenes.narration: But a speech alone cannot reach millions. Every buyer earned a commission for each friend they signed up. [PAUSE 0.6s] The real product was the next recruit.
scenes.visual_intent: A recruitment tree spreads downward while the money from every new buyer climbs to the top.
scenes.visualMetaphor: A recruitment tree grows downward; money climbs every branch to a single crown at the top.

facts.claim: OneCoin members bought OneCoin packages and were paid commissions for recruiting others to buy packages, a pyramid scheme.

scenes.narration: Until October 2017, when Ruja boarded a flight from Sofia to Athens, [PAUSE 0.9s] and vanished.
scenes.visual_intent: The founder's flight path draws across the sea and the signal disappears before it lands.
scenes.visualMetaphor: A boarding pass tears in two as a flight line draws Sofia to Athens and the radar blip fades.

facts.claim: On 25 October 2017 Ruja Ignatova boarded a flight from Sofia to Athens and has not been seen since.

scenes.narration: So OneCoin never needed a blockchain. It needed believers, and it paid them to find more.
scenes.visual_intent: Belief outweighs technology: signed-up believers tip the scale against an empty blockchain block.
scenes.visualMetaphor: A pair of scales: a heavy pile of signed believers outweighs an empty blockchain block.

scenes.narration: In 2022 the FBI put Ruja Ignatova on its Ten Most Wanted list. She was never found. [PAUSE 0.6s] Neither was the coin.
scenes.visual_intent: A case file closes on a fugitive and an empty coin outline: neither was ever found.
scenes.visualMetaphor: A case file slides in, a WANTED stamp lands, then an empty coin outline is stamped NOT FOUND.

facts.claim: In 2022 the FBI added Ruja Ignatova to its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list.
Ignatova has not been found since boarding the October 2017 flight (as of the January 2023 report).
